output.summary: 7 weeks in, +1.22% cumulative alpha vs SPY but -2.37% absolute; win rate only 28.6% weekly and 26% at the pick level. The book is being carried by MU (+49%) and disciplined avoidance of WMT/META/TSLA, but repeatedly gets hurt buying "clean cross-signal" names at RSI extension right before mean-reversion (AVGO -14.5%, MSFT -11.8%, SMCI -12.9%, NVDA -12.9%).
what_worked: Hard-veto insider-cluster rules paid off: avoiding WMT (Walton $313M/$535M), META (COO/CLO cluster), and TSLA saved material downside — every one of these bear theses proved out.

Tax-loss harvesting discipline: closing NVDA 6/29, MSFT 6/8, AVGO 6/15, SMCI 6/15, AMZN/GOOGL/BRK.B/XLE 6/1 booked losses at the right time and generated ~$44 in tax credits while freeing capital for the cyclical rotation.

The 6/22 rotation call (XLI ADD, IWM OPEN, UNH TRIM on macro_mismatch) delivered +1.38% alpha the following week — the cleanest structural win. Trusting the macro_mismatch hard rule on UNH was correct.
MU held through 6/22 despite RSI 69/news 92 warning signs — refusing to add at extension but not panicking out was the right sizing choice; it became the best pick (+49%).
what_missed: Chasing 'best technical composite' megacaps at local tops: MSFT opened 6/1 at technical 82/news 87 → -11.8% in one week. AVGO opened same day, tech 80/news 92 → -14.5%. High technical + high news scores near market highs have been a contrarian sell signal, not a buy signal.

NVDA sizing was too generous given the $221M director sale flag on 6/8. Adding on 5/25 and only closing 6/29 cost -12.9% on a large weight. Insider distribution >$100M should downgrade conviction one full notch, not just cap size.
AAPL opened 6/8 into WWDC 'catalyst' with RSI overbought — -6% in a week. Event-driven opens on already-extended names remain a losing pattern (this is now the 3rd instance).
SMCI 5/25 open at technical 91/news 96 → -12.9% before close. Same pattern: peak-score, high-vol semis at extension.

Weekly win rate 28.6% and by-conviction medium picks are -2.2% avg — too many medium-conviction 'diversifier' opens (XLE, BRK.B, GOOGL, AMZN on 5/18 cold-start) all lost 4-5% in week 1. Cold-start diversification did not protect capital.
lessons_for_pm: Do NOT open new longs when technical score ≥80 AND RSI ≥70 AND news polarity ≥0.90 — this exact combo has produced 4 straight losers averaging -11%. That is exit liquidity, not a signup sheet. Wait for a pullback to MA20 or a lower-RSI re-test.
Insider selling >$100M cluster is a hard size cap of ≤3% weight, regardless of how clean the technicals look. NVDA's $221M director sale should have driven a TRIM on 6/8, not a HOLD.
Medium-conviction 'diversifier' opens have -2.2% avg return over 14 picks. Stop opening medium-conviction names just to spread risk — either high conviction or cash. Concentrate.

High-conviction picks have +2.4% avg and 33% win rate vs medium -2.2%/21% — the edge IS in the conviction filter. Require ≥3 aligned cross-signals AND non-extended tape before assigning high conviction.

Event catalysts (WWDC, earnings prints) on already-overbought names are NOT reasons to open — AAPL 6/8, MU 6/22 (avoided add correctly), NVDA 5/18 all show the same pattern. Buy the setup, not the catalyst.
Rotation-ETF adds (XLF, XLI, IWM, DIA) when macro-regime-favored have been the most reliable positive-alpha trades. Prefer these over single-name megacap opens when tape is choppy.
watch_for: Any new candidate showing RSI ≥70 + news polarity ≥0.90 + technical ≥80 — this triple is a documented loser pattern (MSFT, AVGO, SMCI, AAPL). Flag it as a fade, not a buy.
Insider cluster sales >$100M appearing in this week's data — apply hard size cap or veto, don't rationalize with 'strong news'.
Whether the cyclical rotation (XLF/XLI/IWM/V) is still leading or rolling over — if RSI on XLI/XLF has extended past 65 with news polarity fading, take the win and trim rather than add.
